land.text: the Kingdom of Tlemcen: 'On the collapse of the Almohad Caliphate's rule around 1236 ... the Kingdom of Tlemcen became independent under the rule of the Zayyanids'

predecessors.note: The infobox gives 'Founded: 1235'; the body and the ruler table give 1236.

land.text: Tlemcen and the Zayyanid kingdom: Hasan Corso 'installed an Ottoman governor there and ended the Zayyanid dynasty' in 1551

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps a Zayyanid row to 1555 and the infobox gives 'Deposition: 1557'.

land.text: Oran, where the last Zayyanid ruler fled 'under Spanish protection'

successors.note: Oran was Spanish from 1509 (Spanish Oran page); Mers el-Kebir from 1505.

capitals.name: Tlemcen
capitals.note: The page does not use the word 'capital' but calls the state 'the Kingdom of Tlemcen' 'centered on the town of Tlemcen' (title 'Sultan of Tlemcen'). Under the Marinid occupations (1337-1348, 1352-1359) there was no Zayyanid seat in the city.

rulers.name: Abu Hammu I
rulers.note: Assassinated by his son Abu Tashufin I.

rulers.name: Abu Tashufin I
rulers.note: Until May 1336; the first Marinid conquest follows (1337-1348).

rulers.name: Abu Said Uthman II
rulers.note: Co-ruler with Abu Thabit I after the first Marinid conquest.

rulers.name: Abu Thabit I
rulers.note: Co-ruler with Abu Said Uthman II.

rulers.name: Abu Hammu II Musa
rulers.note: First reign, from February 1359 after the second Marinid conquest (1352-1359).

rulers.name: Abu Hammu II Musa
rulers.note: Second reign; expedition to Bugia defeated, 1366.

rulers.name: Abu Malek I
rulers.note: First reign; the Hafsid page has him beaten by Abu Faris in 1424.

rulers.name: Abu Abdallah II
rulers.note: First reign; then an interregnum and civil war (1427-1429).

rulers.name: Al Hassan ibn Abdallah (Hasan al-Abdallah)
rulers.note: Table: 1550-1557. 'By 1551, the Ottomans had occupied Tlemcen and the last Zayyanid ruler ... fled to Oran under Spanish protection and died a few years later': a ruler in exile after 1551. [Review af-02-d: to set to 1551, the end of the state (Zayyanid page: By 1551, the Ottomans had occupied Tlemcen); the table row runs to 1557 in exile.]

keyframe_review.note: 125,839 km2 (Algeria's west and centre, 2.12 W to 4.67 E, 33.5-36.9 N; 159 Oranais cells). The page has no infobox area, so no comparison is possible. The eastern part (Algiers) overlaps what the Hafsid page has annexed in 1235 ('Algiers ... as far as the Chelif River'); unverified beyond Tlemcen within the page budget.

Shape unchanged (126,172 km2) but it holds 1285-1336 only: 'In May 1337, after a two-year siege, Tlemcen finally fell to a Marinid assault' (Abu al-Hasan page) and the ruler table has the 'First Marinid conquest (1337-1348)'. Cliopatria shows the kingdom as Zayyanid to 1343 and as Marinid from 1344 (Marinid 514,751 km2 shape). From 1337 the ledger hatches it as Marinid-occupied.

correction.text: the Kingdom of Tlemcen as in Cliopatria's 1285 shape, with the Marinid occupations of 1337-1348 and 1352-1359 in the ledger

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1344-1362, a gap in Cliopatria's row (the Marinid shape of 1344-1351 and 1352-1362 covers it). The page: 'a Marinid occupation of Tlemcen between 1337 and 1359 (with an interruption from 1348 to 1352)'; the ruler table: Abu Said Uthman II and Abu Thabit I 1348-1352, Abu Hammu II from February 1359. The kingdom is drawn as Zayyanid with the Marinid occupations (1344-1347, 1352-1358) as ledger events; the Zayyanids hold the same land in 1348-1351 and from 1359.

126,172 km2, the same kingdom: 'Under the long reign of Abu Hammu II (r. 1359-1389)' a 'third period of political strength'. The Hafsid page has Abu Faris annex Algiers in 1410-1411 (the shape keeps it Zayyanid) and defeat the Zayyanid sultan in 1424 (client, not annexation).

125,146 km2: six cells at Oran/Mers el-Kebir (35.5-35.8 N, 0.9-0.3 W) leave the shape in 1507. The Mers el-Kebir page: 'The Spanish ... captured it in 1505 under Cardinal Cisneros'; the Spanish Oran page and the Regency of Algiers page: Oran conquered from the Zayyanids in 1509. Cliopatria's 1507 is between the two.

124,099 km2: three more cells near Cherchell/Tipaza (36.5 N, 2.0-2.4 E) leave in 1512 and return in 1519; no page opened explains them (the Spanish Oran page has only the 1509 conquest and the 1707-1792 history). Treat as Cliopatria noise.
125,019 km2: the cells lost in 1512 return in 1519, a year after 'Aruj was killed after the Spanish-backed siege of Tlemcen' (May 1518) and the Zayyanids' restoration. The Regency page has no area.

125,121 km2, unchanged in substance, but the Regency page has the Ottomans of Algiers installing 'an Ottoman governor' at Tlemcen in 1551, the Zayyanid page 'By 1551, the Ottomans had occupied Tlemcen': the shape holds 1521-1550.

correction.text: belongs to the Ottoman Regency of Algiers for 1552-1555

keyframe_review.note: The Zayyanid state ended in 1551: Hasan Corso 'drove them [the Saadians] out. He installed an Ottoman governor there and ended the Zayyanid dynasty' (Regency of Algiers page); 'the last Zayyanid ruler, Hasan al-Abdallah, fled to Oran under Spanish protection' (Zayyanid page). The shape for 1552-1555 belongs to the Regency of Algiers; the infobox's 'Deposition: 1557' dates only the last ruler's reign in exile.

ledger.note: 1236: the Kingdom of Tlemcen becomes independent under Yaghmurasen. 'On the collapse of the Almohad Caliphate's rule around 1236 ... the Kingdom of Tlemcen became independent under the rule of the Zayyanids'; the table starts the founder in 1236, the infobox says 'Founded: 1235'.
1242: the Hafsids take Tlemcen. 'In 1242, he captured Tlemcen from the Zayyanids.' The Zayyanid page has the kingdom 'intermittently a vassal of Hafsid Ifriqiya'; no page dates the end.
1249: the Hafsid hold on Tlemcen ends, bridging. The page is silent; 5 October 1249 is Abu Zakariya's death in the Hafsid ruler table.
1299: the Marinids besiege Tlemcen. Timeline: 'Beginning of Tlemcen's siege by the Marinids, which will last nine years.'

1307: the siege of Tlemcen ends. 'After an eight-year siege of Tlemcen by the Marinids that ended in 1307' (the Marinid timeline says nine years); Abu Zayyan I's reign ends on 14 April 1308 (table) and the reigns of Abu Hammu I and Abu Tashufin I mark a 'second political apogee'.

May 1337: Tlemcen falls to Abu al-Hasan's Marinids. 'In May 1337, after a two-year siege, Tlemcen finally fell to a Marinid assault'; 'In 1337 the Abdalwadid kingdom of Tlemcen was conquered' (Marinid page). The page speaks of the city; the whole kingdom is the researcher's reading.

1348: the Zayyanids return to Tlemcen. The first Marinid conquest ran 1337-1348 ('with an interruption from 1348 to 1352'); Abu Said Uthman II and Abu Thabit I rule together 1348-1352 (Abu al-Hasan page: 'The Zayyanid Abu Sa'id Uthman II was proclaimed king of Tlemcen').
1352: Abu Inan retakes Tlemcen. 'In 1352 Abu Inan Faris recaptured Tlemcen'; the Zayyanid page dates the second Marinid occupation 1352-1359.

1359: Abu Hammu II restores the kingdom. 'A Marinid occupation of Tlemcen between 1337 and 1359'; the table starts Abu Hammu II Musa in February 1359 and the 'third period of political strength' under his reign (1359-1389); Marinid attempts to retake Tlemcen continue 'up to 1370'.

1424: the Zayyanid kingdom becomes a Hafsid client (mirror of the Hafsid dossier). 'In 1424, he defeated the Zayyanid sultan, Abu Malik Abd al-Wahid', who 'was eventually replaced by yet another Zayyanid relative with Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz's help in 1431'; the Zayyanid page has the kingdom 'intermittently a vassal of Hafsid Ifriqiya'.
1434: Hafsid influence over Tlemcen ends, bridging. The Hafsid page is silent on the end; 1434 is the end of Abu Faris's reign.

region.text: Mers el-Kebir, the port of Oran

ledger.note: 1505: Spain takes Mers el-Kebir. 'The Spanish, who named it Mazalquivir, captured it in 1505 under Cardinal Cisneros.' The page says only that the port 'fell under the rulers of the Kingdom of Tlemcen in the 13th century' and does not name the Zayyanids.

1509: Spain conquers Oran. The Spanish Oran page infobox: 'Spanish conquest: 1509', carried out 'on the Kingdom of Tlemcen'; the Regency of Algiers page: 'The Spanish conquered Oran from the Zayyanids.'

June 1517: Aruj (Oruc) Barbarossa takes Tenes. 'Aruj took Tenes after defeating Hamid bin Abid in June'; he is said to have entered Tlemcen in 1518 (Boaziz; disputed by Julien). The page does not say that Tenes was Zayyanid; the Chlef unit is the researcher's reading.
May 1518: Aruj dies at Tlemcen. 'Aruj was killed after the Spanish-backed siege of Tlemcen'; the gates opened 'for the Spanish in May 1518'.

1551: the Ottomans of Algiers take Tlemcen and the Zayyanid kingdom ends. The Saadians invaded Tlemcen and 'Hasan Corso drove them out. He installed an Ottoman governor there and ended the Zayyanid dynasty'; 'By 1551, the Ottomans had occupied Tlemcen' (Zayyanid page), whose last ruler fled to Oran under Spanish protection. Cliopatria ends the row in 1555 and the infobox gives 1557.

wars.name: Marinid siege of Tlemcen
wars.outcome: The siege (eight or nine years) ends in 1307 without a conquest; the reigns of Abu Hammu I and Abu Tashufin I (1308-1337) then mark a 'second political apogee'.
wars.note: Marinid page: 'Beginning of Tlemcen's siege by the Marinids, which will last nine years' (1299).

wars.name: Marinid conquest of Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Marinid victory: invaded early 1335, siege suspended 1336 or 1337, Tlemcen falls in May 1337.

wars.name: Second Marinid conquest of Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Marinid occupation from Abu Inan's retaking of Tlemcen in 1352 to Abu Hammu II's restoration in February 1359.

wars.name: Hafsid conquests of Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Hafsid captures of Tlemcen in 1242 and a defeat of the Zayyanid sultan in 1424; a Zayyanid relative installed with Hafsid help in 1431.

wars.name: Spanish conquests of Mers el-Kebir and Oran
Oruc's and Spain's war for Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Aruj takes Tenes (June 1517) and is killed after a Spanish-backed siege of Tlemcen (May 1518).

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Hasan Corso expels the Saadians, installs a governor and ends the dynasty in 1551; the last Zayyanid flees to Oran.
wars.note: 'Spain and the Ottoman Regency of Algiers fought over control of Tlemcen' (Zayyanid page).

certainty.note: No treaty line is given by any page: the Moulouya frontier with the Marinids, the Algiers frontier with the Hafsids and the Saharan edge are approximate. Tlemcen, Oran and Mers el-Kebir are firm points.

notes: CLIOPATRIA. (1) The row has a hole 1344-1362 filled by the Marinid rows (514,751 km2 and 737,941 km2); the pages have the Marinids occupying Tlemcen 1337-1348 and 1352-1359 and the Zayyanids ruling 1348-1352 and from 1359, so a new keyframe holds the kingdom for 1344-1362 and the occupations are ledger events. (2) The row ends in 1555, the infobox gives 'Deposition: 1557', the Regency of Algiers and the Zayyanid page have the Ottomans in Tlemcen by 1551: end set at 1551. (3) Cliopatria's 1507 and 1512 cells (Oran area, then three cells near Cherchell) and its 1519 return of those cells are only partly explained (Mers el-Kebir 1505, Oran 1509). AREA. The Zayyanid page gives no area figure; no comparison was possible. NOT SETTLED. The Hafsid, Marinid and Aragonese vassalages ('intermittently a vassal of Hafsid Ifriqiya, Marinid Morocco, or Aragon') are undated on the page except the Hafsid events of 1242 and 1424-1431 (mirrored here as an occupation and a client period); the Spanish protectorate over Tlemcen after 1509 and the Saadian invasion of 1551 (Regency of Algiers page; the Zayyanid page does not mention the Saadians); the Zayyanid status of Ténès in 1517; how far east the kingdom reached against the Hafsid claim to Algiers. The ruler table's last row (1550-1557) is a ruler in exile after 1551.
